overview.verdictSnippet: The Kona long range dive charter from Kona Honu Divers is a 7-hour, 2-tank trip on a 6-diver catamaran to South Kona lava tubes or northern arches, with free Nitrox and a boxed lunch from $269. It suits experienced divers with 25+ logged dives; the main drawbacks are the strict entry requirements and a no-refund window of 72 hours.

Maximum 6 divers on the Honu Lele, a 33-foot World Cat power catamaran that the operator says is usually the only boat at these sites
Nitrox fills, tanks, weights, a guide and a boxed lunch are included in the $269 base price
Entry bar is high: at least 25 logged dives, a dive within the last 6 months, a dive computer and 60 minutes of air on an 80 cf tank
The same boat can be paired with the operator's Blackwater Night Dive on the same day, with about 3 hours between trips
whatToExpect: Check in at the Honu Lele slip at Honokohau Harbor (74-425 Kealakehe Parkway) for an 8:00 am departure; the trip runs until about 3:00 pm.

The captain picks north or south based on sea conditions, then runs the coast at speed on the 33-foot catamaran; the operator says dolphins, pilot whales and, in winter, hammerheads are sometimes seen on the way.

A boxed lunch is served on board during the surface interval; the operator's own page also calls it a 'full lunch', so expect something between the two.
Dive two is at a second site in the same area, for example a drift around Kaiwi Point when conditions allow.
The boat returns to Honokohau Harbor by about 3:00 pm; the operator asks you not to fly or drive above 2,000 feet for 18 hours afterwards.

verdict.intro: At $269 plus roughly 14% in taxes and fees, this charter is worth it for certified divers who already meet the 25-dive and 60-minute-air thresholds and want sites that the 2-tank local boats do not reach. It is not a good fit for anyone who has not been in the water in the last 6 months, because the operator will turn you away. The 72-hour no-refund rule means you should book it only once your travel dates are fixed.

The last stop is 30 minutes at Punaluu Black Sand Beach, where green sea turtles often rest, before the drive back to Hilo for a 3:00 PM drop-off.

faq.a: The Winona runs two Coral Gardens snorkel sails: a morning departure at 9:00 AM with 8:30 AM check-in and an afternoon departure at 1:00 PM with 12:30 PM check-in, each about 3 hours. Both leave from the north dock of Maalaea Harbor at 233 Maalaea Rd. Mornings are usually calmer.

faq.q: Is the Coral Gardens sail good for beginners and children?
faq.a: The trip includes a beginner snorkel class, flotation devices for everyone in the water and a shallow, sheltered reef, which makes it one of the easier Maui snorkel sails for first-timers and children. A child fare covers ages 5 to 12, and infants need a parent-supplied life vest. The boat itself is not wheelchair accessible.

faq.q: What is included in the snorkel sail price?
faq.a: The fare covers snorkel gear and flotation, a beginner lesson, a light breakfast on the morning sail or lunch on the afternoon sail, appetizers, an open bar with beer and cocktails plus soft drinks, juice and water, music and the captain and crew. Hotel transport, parking validation and gratuity are not included.

faq.q: What is the cancellation policy for the Winona snorkel sail?
faq.a: Groups of up to 4 get a full refund with 24 hours' notice, groups of 5 or more need 48 hours, and private charters need 7 days, according to the Greetwell listing. If the operator cancels for weather, mechanical issues or low bookings you can rebook or take a full refund. The operator's own terms page states no exact deadline.
